description: A single table rendered as an image, with six column headers — Alloy, Phases present, Phase fraction of B2 (%), Average grain size (μm), Twin fraction (%), Composition of phases (wt%) — and three data rows. The accompanying caption reads "Table 2 Microstructural features observed in the three alloys under hot-rolled conditions", while the in-block header line reads "Table 3". Row 1, alloy 28Mn0Ni: phases "γ + κ", B2 fraction ~0.5%, average grain size 5.6 ± 2.3 μm, twin fraction 28%, γ composition Fe-27.5Mn-7.9Al. Row 2, alloy 28Mn5Ni: "γ + κ + intergranular B2 particles + DO3", B2 ~4%, grain size 6.9 ± 1.7 μm, twins 40%, γ Fe-27.8Mn-7.5Al-5.7Ni and B2 Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni. Row 3, alloy 15Mn5Ni: "γ + κ + intergranular B2 particles + B2 stringers + DO3", B2 ~12%, grain size 5.7 ± 1.3 μm, twins printed as "07"%, γ Fe-14Mn-7.6Al-4.9Ni and B2 Fe-10.1Mn-9.7Al-8.3Ni. The table quantifies that Ni addition raises the B2 fraction (~0.5 → ~4 → ~12%) and the twin fraction, and that the B2 phase in the higher-Mn alloy is richer in Ni, Al and Mn, i.e. solute partitioning between γ and B2.

observations.observation: The table has six columns: Alloy, Phases present, Phase fraction of B2 (%), Average grain size (μm), Twin fraction (%), Composition of phases (wt%).
Phase fraction of B2 increases with Ni addition and lower Mn: ~0.5% for 28Mn0Ni, ~4% for 28Mn5Ni and ~12% for 15Mn5Ni.
Average grain size is 5.6 ± 2.3 μm (28Mn0Ni), 6.9 ± 1.7 μm (28Mn5Ni) and 5.7 ± 1.3 μm (15Mn5Ni), so 28Mn5Ni has the coarsest grains.
Twin fraction is 28% for 28Mn0Ni and 40% for 28Mn5Ni, while the 15Mn5Ni entry is printed as '07'.
Phase assemblage of 28Mn0Ni is γ + κ only, whereas 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni additionally contain intergranular B2 particles and DO3; 15Mn5Ni further contains B2 stringers.
γ composition is Fe-27.5Mn-7.9Al (28Mn0Ni), Fe-27.8Mn-7.5Al-5.7Ni (28Mn5Ni) and Fe-14Mn-7.6Al-4.9Ni (15Mn5Ni).
B2 composition is Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni in 28Mn5Ni and Fe-10.1Mn-9.7Al-8.3Ni in 15Mn5Ni in wt.%, showing higher Ni, Al and Mn in the B2 phase of the higher-Mn alloy than its γ matrix.
The caption states the table summarises microstructural features observed in the three alloys under hot-rolled conditions.
The caption text and the table header disagree on the table number: the caption block says 'Table 2' while the table itself is headed 'Table 3'.

The citing text states that the microstructural features (grain size, twin boundary and B2 volume fraction) and the TEM-EDS elemental analysis of B2 particles/stringers and adjacent γ-matrix grains of all three alloys are summarised in this table.
The citing text states that the B2 forming alloys show a general trend of higher Ni, Al and Mn concentrations in the B2 phase with increasing Mn content of the alloy.
The citing text states that EDS elemental analysis in both SEM and TEM suggests clear solute partitioning between γ and B2 phases in the LDS alloy.
